title: Test AA batteries with a voltmeter and sort by voltage
instruction: Use the two loose voltmeter probes to test all 5 AA batteries. Keep the probe tips touching opposite terminals of the same battery for at least 0.50 seconds. Use the magnitude of the displayed voltage: put batteries reading 1.20 V or more in the green ALIVE bin and lower readings in the red DEAD bin. Leave every battery released inside its bin.
context: Bench inspection combines a two-probe electrical measurement with a sorting decision for visually identical cells. ALIVE and DEAD denote the stated voltage cutoff, not remaining capacity.
setup: One fixed layout on the standard calibrated YAM station: a 1100 x 1300 x 60 mm table with top at world z=0.7475 m; two parallel-gripper arms at (0,+/-0.305,0.75) m; standard overhead and two wrist RGB cameras. Coordinates are metres: x forward from the arm bases, +y to the robot's left; apparatus heights below are relative to the table top. Five identical unbranded AA cells, each 14.5 mm diameter, 50.5 mm overall and 23 g, with steel terminals and blue insulating polymer wrap, start at x=0.16,0.21,0.26,0.31,0.36, y=0, height=54 mm, positive ends along +y. Each cell has two fixed rubber V saddles 16.5 mm either side of its midpoint along y; each saddle has a 30 x 6 x 40 mm support and two 14 x 6 x 4 mm faces inclined 45 degrees. Red and black loose handheld probes are each 152 mm long and 28 g, with 70 mm long, 16 mm diameter insulated handles, 24 mm guards, 50 mm insulated noses, 28 mm bare steel shafts and 1.5 mm radius rounded tips. Handle centres start at (0.11,+0.30,0.0603) and (0.11,-0.30,0.0603), respectively, pointing inward. Each handle rests on two fixed 22 x 6 x 52 mm rubber blocks 46 mm apart. A fixed yellow polymer DC voltmeter, 165 x 250 x 35 mm, stands at (0.525,0,0), with a live signed two-decimal display, preset voltage mode and two 3 mm insulated visual leads connected to the probe handles. Fixed green ALIVE and red DEAD polymer bins, each 220 x 180 x 70 mm with 210 x 170 mm inner openings, 6 mm floor, 5 mm walls and raised labels, stand at (0.26,+0.30,0) and (0.26,-0.30,0). Both arms start in the standard ready pose with open grippers. See setup.png and scene_inventory.json for the exact layout.
scoring: Both probe tips must contact opposite exposed terminals of the same cell continuously for 0.50 s. The simulator requires at least 0.005 N mean native normal contact force on that cell over 50 ms from each probe, with at most 0.6 mm electrical contact-surface tolerance. Reversed polarity is allowed; use magnitude. Values >= 1.20 V belong in ALIVE and lower values in DEAD. Each measured cell earns 1/5 in the current final state when its complete native cell envelope is inside the correct 210x170 mm bin opening, between the floor and rim, with 1 mm contact tolerance on every boundary, linear speed <=25 mm/s, angular speed <=0.8 rad/s, and every robot collision envelope >=15 mm away. Unmeasured, misplaced, held, moving or partially contained cells earn zero. All 5 must satisfy these conditions for 1.00 s for success. Any battery/probe envelope leaving x=-0.19..0.91 m, y=-0.65..0.65 m, z=table-top-15 mm..1.80 m, or any nonfinite object state, permanently sets the whole trial to zero.
reset_notes: Restore the fixed initial poses and preset voltages; no consumables and no object jitter.
fidelity: Native 240 Hz PhysX rigid-body cells and loose probes; two-probe reading requires physical contacts and terminal geometry. Ideal constant DC cell voltages and high-impedance meter; no chemistry, discharge, internal resistance, noise or deformable damage. Leads are massless noncolliding visual curves. Instrument display changes only visually. No runtime object teleportation or attachments.
